doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: La Rocca and the jazz-origin dispute
title: Tiger Rag and Livery Stable Blues authorship
summary: Discussion of Tiger Rag played by Laine's men long before La Rocca, credited to Nunez and others, and the Chicago and New York copyright fight.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you play Tiger Rag then with your band long before La Rocca, you say? Sure.
He called out a Liberty Stable Blues, I believe, or something like that is.
No, I believe that's something else. No, that was something else, I think. That's something else, Stable Blues.
That was Yellis, Yellis too, and Yellis and Paquet.
That's the ones for Tiger Rag, Paquet and Yellen Nunes. They made it up, you think?
They had a big cold scramble in Chicago, New York. Oh, I read about that. You remember that? Yeah. Had him, had, I'll see, have a Yellen Nunes arrested.
Well, that's just how that happened, you see? Now, of course, uh... But he is a liar.
